deckTitle: Multi-Tenant Agentic AI on Google Cloud: Reference Taxonomy & 5-Hop Governance (Workstream 1)
deckSubtitle: Solving the SaaS AI Dilemma: Prevent tool-schema leaks and rogue-tenant quota starvation using Agent Development Kit (ADK), Model Context Protocol (MCP) & Agent Registry Discovery (ARD) across Pooled, Silo & Hybrid tiers
tldr: Why It Matters (The SaaS AI Dilemma): Dedicated projects per Standard tenant erode SaaS gross margins, whereas naive shared agents leak cross-tenant data via tool schemas and let one rogue tenant starve shared LLM rate limits.
Core Primitives (ADK • MCP • ARD): ADK (OS syscall scheduler), MCP (POSIX tool driver ABI) & ARD (chrooted VFS catalog) isolate every tenant turn across 5 cryptographic hops.

Three Topologies & 80/20 Code Reuse: Pattern A (Pooled RLS + 90% prefix cache), Pattern B (Sovereign Silo VPC-SC + CMEK), and Pattern C (Dynamic Hybrid PSC + 0ms tier upgrade) share 80% identical Python ADK code.

5-Hop Pipeline (~42ms p95 Overhead): Enforces KMS-signed STS JWTs (<0.15ms cached JWKS verify), ARD pruning, targeted Valkey SCAN+UNLINK L1 eviction, streaming Model Armor/DLP (~22ms), and AlloyDB FORCE RLS.

Architecture Center & GitHub Kit: Ships 14 Official (#78) blueprints, 27 runnable files (core-cymbal-agent/ (27-File Workbench)), feature-flagged EAP compensating controls (GAP-01..05), and 12/12 forensic + 107/107 runtime assertions.

bullets: Agentic AI & Foundation Models: Vertex AI Agent Engine (ADK runtime, Agent Registry & L1–L5 Memory Bank), Gemini 2.5 Pro with ContextCacheConfig (90% shared prefix discount), Vertex AI Model Garden (Dedicated PT), and Gemma 3 (27B) on private GKE.

Ingress, Identity & AI Safety Guardrails: Global External Application Load Balancer, Google Cloud Armor L7 WAF, Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) & IAM Security Token Service (RFC 8693 OBO + RFC 9449 DPoP), Vertex AI Model Armor, and Cloud Sensitive Data Protection (DLP).

Data, Storage, Networking & Governance: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL (FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY), Memorystore for Valkey (per-tenant RPM bulkheads & JTI deny-list) & Firestore, VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC) & Private Service Connect (PSC), Cloud KMS CMEK, and BigQuery OTel.

Shared 80% Reusable Application Core: All three isolation patterns execute the exact same Python ADK 5-hop security pipeline (`core-cymbal-agent/runtime_pipeline.py`), parameterizing only the surrounding 20% Google Cloud project and network boundary.

sections.heading: Design alternatives — Compensating Controls for EAP Product Gaps (GAP-01..05)
tableRows:
GAP-01 (Hop 2)
Agent Engine Registry
Shared Agent Engine Registry lacks native per-tenant IAM condition predicates on `ListAgents` discovery calls.
`Hop2RegistryPDP.authorize_agent_and_prune_tools` filters ARD by signed JWT `tenant_id` + ADK `before_agent_callback` pruning.
WS2 Test 2 PASS (`HTTP 403` on cross-tenant Agent Alpha probe) • Sunset at Native GA: Feature-Flagged Native Hook

GAP-02 (Hop 3)
Memory Bank CMEK
Pooled Vertex AI Memory Bank supports project-level CMEK rather than distinct per-tenant KMS keys in one shared pool.
Envelope encryption + `<5s` tenant-prefixed Valkey `SCAN+UNLINK` (`cache:{tenant_id}:*`) on KMS disable (`<60s` `HTTP 423`) + `SET NX` single-flight re-hydration.
WS3 Tests 4A/4B/6 PASS (`HTTP 423 Locked` <60s, 0 peer cache evictions) • Sunset at GA: Feature-Flagged Native Hook

GAP-03 (Hop 3)
Per-Tenant Rate Quotas
Vertex AI quota system enforces regional project-level RPM/TPM limits rather than native per-tenant sub-quotas.
`Hop3ComputeFinOpsBulkhead` enforces atomic Lua token-bucket RPM limits in Valkey (`120` vs. `600` RPM, `HTTP 429 Retry-After`) + `4k/8k` thinking clamps.
WS2 Test 6 PASS (`HTTP 429` on 500-RPM flood; budget clamped to 4k) • Sunset at GA: Feature-Flagged Native Hook

GAP-04 (Hop 1/4)
Multi-IdP 3LO Broker
External Microsoft Entra ID OIDC tokens require claims normalization and anti-confused-deputy isolation for 3LO MCP tools.
Hop 1 normalizes Entra `tid`/`sub` into DPoP-bound `{tenant}:{user}` 3LO token vaults with `-32042` step-up consent & `dpop_jkt` verification.
WS2 Test 10 & 10-SaaS Matrix PASS (`HTTP 401` step-up -> `200 OK` ServiceNow) • Sunset at GA: Feature-Flagged Native Hook

GAP-05 (Hop 5)
Zero-PII Token Billing
Cloud Billing exports aggregate Vertex AI SKU charges by GCP project rather than individual logical SaaS `tenant_id`.
`Hop5DataPlaneRLSAndOTel` streams SHA-256 zero-PII OTel spans to BigQuery (`SELECT tenant_id, SUM(cached_tokens*0.1 + thinking_tokens) GROUP BY tenant_id`).
Forensic Check F-08 PASS (BigQuery OTel chargeback SQL verified) • Sunset at GA: Feature-Flagged Native Hook

sections.heading: Design considerations — 5-Hop Cryptographic Verification Pipeline

pipelineSteps.title: Perimeter WAF, Federated OIDC & DPoP Token Binding
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Strips unauthenticated X-Tenant-Id headers at the L7 load balancer, verifies Google Workspace or Microsoft Entra ID OIDC JWTs, and exchanges credentials via RFC 8693 OBO.
pipelineSteps.invariant: KMS ECDSA P-256 JWT + Local JWKS Cache (<0.15ms verify)
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 401 on Spoofed Header, Replayed DPoP or Revoked JTI

pipelineSteps.title: Tenant-Scoped Agent & MCP Tool Catalog Filtering
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Evaluates the signed TenantSecurityContext against Agent Engine Registry metadata before LLM tool-binding, returning only shared platform tools and tenant-owned private agents.
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 403 Forbidden on Cross-Tenant Agent or MCP Discovery

pipelineSteps.title: gVisor Sandbox, L1–L5 Memory & Valkey Bulkheads
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Executes tool subprocesses in gVisor (runsc) sandboxes, partitions L1–L5 Memory Bank namespaces, and enforces Valkey RPM bulkheads and targeted SCAN+UNLINK CMEK eviction.
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 429 on RPM Burst • <5s Targeted L1 Eviction on CMEK Revoke

pipelineSteps.title: Streaming Model Armor Screening & Sensitive Data Redaction
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Screens ingress prompts and streaming completion chunks via regional gRPC callouts (~22ms p95) for prompt injection, tenant Natural Language Constraints (NLCs), and PII/IBAN/PAN tokens.
pipelineSteps.invariant: Policy: Regional gRPC inspectContent + Tenant NLC Rules
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 400 on Prompt Injection • HTTP 422 on NLC Policy Breach

pipelineSteps.title: Transactional Row-Level Security, CMEK & BigQuery OTel SQL
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Binds parameterized PostgreSQL session context (app.current_tenant_id) for FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, verifies Cloud KMS CMEK liveness, and streams zero-PII OTel spans to BigQuery.
pipelineSteps.invariant: SQL: SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id • OTel Chargeback SQL
pipelineSteps.gate: 0 Unauthorized Rows • HTTP 423 Locked on CMEK Revocation

bullets: Hop 1 — Edge WAF & Cached JWKS Identity (~8ms p95): Cloud Armor strips spoofed X-Tenant-Id headers while IAP and IAM STS mint a KMS-signed OBO + DPoP TenantSecurityContext verified locally in <0.15ms.
Hop 2 — Registry Discovery Filtering (~4ms p95): Vertex AI Agent Engine Registry evaluates tenant visibility metadata prior to tool binding, returning HTTP 403 on unauthorized private agents.

Hop 3 — gVisor Runtime, Valkey Bulkheads & Targeted Eviction (~3ms p95): Isolates L1–L5 Memory Bank namespaces, clamps RPM (120/600) and thinking budgets (4k/8k), and evicts only cache:{tenant_id}:* on CMEK revoke.

Hop 4 — Streaming Model Armor & DLP (~22ms p95): Regional gRPC Model Armor + Sensitive Data Protection blocks prompt injection (HTTP 400) and semantic NLC violations (HTTP 422) with <2.5% impact on turn TTFT.

Hop 5 — Transactional RLS, CMEK & BigQuery OTel SQL (~5ms p95): AlloyDB enforces SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id Row-Level Security, Cloud KMS validates CMEK liveness (HTTP 423), and BigQuery aggregates zero-PII OTel spans.

sections.heading: Design considerations — Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework Alignment
bullets: 1. Security, Privacy & Compliance: Enforces zero-trust defense-in-depth across all 5 hops—combining <0.15ms cached-JWKS DPoP verification, per-user 3LO vaults against Confused Deputy attacks, AlloyDB RLS, and revocable Cloud KMS CMEK.

2. Reliability & Anti-Stampede Resilience: Prevents noisy-neighbor outages via Valkey token-bucket bulkheads, targeted SCAN+UNLINK cache:{tenant_id}:* eviction (0 peer cache misses), and Valkey SET NX single-flight lazy re-hydration.

3. Cost Optimization (FinOps): Shares a 32,000-token immutable system prefix in Gemini 2.5 Pro ContextCacheConfig (90% discount, 84.7% net token savings) and attributes COGS via BigQuery OTel SQL chargeback views.

4. Operational Excellence & 5. Performance (~42ms p95): Reuses 80% of the Python ADK codebase across Terraform 2.6/3.6/4.6, bounds total 5-Hop control-plane overhead to ~42ms p95 (<2.5% TTFT), and gates CI/CD on 12/12 + 107/107 tests.

Welcome everyone. We have structured this streamlined eleven-slide reference architecture briefing into a cohesive five-part engineering series roadmap so you can trace the SaaS AI Dilemma from isolation topologies all the way to automated CI/CD forensic compliance.

In this session, we are walking through our foundational reference architecture for running multi-tenant AI agents on Google Cloud. Right upfront, we define our three core building blocks using operating-system primitives—Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK) as our OS syscall scheduler, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as our POSIX tool driver ABI, and Agent Registry and Discovery (ARD) as our chrooted virtual filesystem catalog—and show how we solve the SaaS AI Architect’s Dilemma: avoiding the margin erosion of spinning up dedicated cloud projects for every small customer while preventing tool-schema data leaks and noisy-neighbor rate starvation in a shared pool.

With our thesis defined on Slide 1, let's turn to Slide 2 for our Agenda and 5-Part Series Navigation table so you can see the exact macro-to-micro flow of the deck.

slideSpeakerNotes.title: Part 1 (Slide 4) — 12-Dimension Multi-Tenant Isolation Decision Matrix
slideSpeakerNotes.whyHere: Building directly on the customer personas from Slide 3, this matrix closes Part 1 by comparing Pooled (Pattern A), Sovereign Silos (Pattern B), and Dynamic Hybrid (Pattern C).
slideSpeakerNotes.whatIsHappening: To serve both ends of that customer spectrum, this twelve-dimension matrix compares Pattern A, our High-Density Shared Pool; Pattern B, our Zero-Trust Sovereign Silos; and Pattern C, our Dynamic Hybrid Bridge. Notice the operational fleet-scale trade-off in the table: managing five hundred enterprise customers in Pattern B means maintaining five hundred separate VPC Service Controls perimeters, KMS keys, and AlloyDB instances—which is why Pattern C hosts nine hundred fifty standard tenants in the shared pool and reserves fifty Private Service Connect spokes for regulated contracts. Also note our kill-switch distinction: while Google Cloud KMS key state propagation can take up to sixty seconds across storage, Hop 3 runs a targeted Valkey SCAN and UNLINK of the tenant’s cache prefix in under five seconds to enforce our HTTP 423 lock SLA.

slideSpeakerNotes.title: Part 2 (Slide 5) — L1 Logical: Reference Taxonomy — 3 Logical Security Layers & Signed STS JWT
slideSpeakerNotes.whyHere: Opening Part 2 on securing the agent loop, Slide 5 establishes the Level 1 Logical view—organizing our architecture into three logical security layers so it maps cleanly onto the four physical VPC-SC perimeters on Slide 6.
slideSpeakerNotes.whatIsHappening: Before we inspect individual cloud services, this Level 1 diagram organizes our entire architecture into three logical security layers from left to right—preventing any terminology clash with the four physical VPC-SC network perimeters on the next slide. Layer 1 on the left verifies federated identity and DPoP proofs at the Cloud Armor and IAP edge. Layer 2 in the center runs our Five-Hop ADK Control Plane, where regional gRPC callouts keep Hop 4 inline Model Armor and Cloud DLP inspection to roughly twenty-two milliseconds and total five-hop control-plane overhead to about forty-two milliseconds at p95. And to prevent security drift during a five-minute STS JWT window, every hop checks a three-millisecond Valkey JTI and CMEK revocation deny-list before routing into Layer 3 on the right.

slideSpeakerNotes.title: Part 3 (Slide 7) — L3 Process: 5-Actor UML Sequence, Fail-Closed Circuit Breakers & Stampede Recovery
slideSpeakerNotes.whyHere: Moving from L2 Physical on Slide 6 to L3 Process on Slide 7, this unified diagram combines our chronological five-actor request sequence with our fail-closed circuit breakers, sub-five-second Valkey SCAN+UNLINK eviction, and SET NX PX 5000 single-flight recovery.
slideSpeakerNotes.whatIsHappening: Now that we have the L1 logical layers and L2 physical perimeters in place, this merged Level 3 process and operational resilience slide traces both the chronological happy path across five actors and every fail-closed circuit breaker in one unified view. Steps 1 through 6 trace a live customer turn in roughly forty-two milliseconds of control-plane overhead. And in the red fail-closed frame at the bottom, spoofed headers or ~3ms JTI revocations return HTTP 401 or 403, rate bursts over 120 or 600 RPM return HTTP 429 with Retry-After jitter, and a revoked Cloud KMS key triggers an HTTP 423 lock with a sub-five-second targeted Valkey SCAN and UNLINK of cache:{tenant}:*—followed by single-flight SET NX PX 5000 lazy re-hydration from AlloyDB RLS when the key is restored.

slideSpeakerNotes.title: Part 2 (Slide 8) — L4 Wire: Spoofed Header Stripping & <0.15ms Cached-JWKS STS JWT
slideSpeakerNotes.whyHere: Completing our L1 → L2 → L3 → L4 macro-to-micro hierarchy, Slide 8 inspects the raw JSON payload on the wire before and after Hop 1 token exchange.
slideSpeakerNotes.whatIsHappening: Zooming all the way down to Level 4, here we open up the wire packet traveling across those hops. On the left, an untrusted client attempts to inject a spoofed X-Tenant-Id header claiming to be FinVault Bank. In the center, Cloud Armor and our Hop 1 Security Token Service strip that header, verify the caller’s OIDC and DPoP proof, and mint a KMS ECDSA P-256 signed STS JWT. On the right, downstream microservices verify that asymmetric signature locally in under 0.15 milliseconds using an in-memory cached JWKS public key—achieving mathematical non-repudiation with zero per-hop KMS network calls.

slideSpeakerNotes.title: Part 4 (Slide 9) — Mind the Gap: GAP-01..05 Compensating Controls & BigQuery OTel SQL
slideSpeakerNotes.whyHere: Part 4 on Slide 9 provides our transparent engineering ledger of five current platform gaps, our codebase compensating controls, and our feature-flagged native adapter sunset hooks.
slideSpeakerNotes.whatIsHappening: This register maps our five compensating production controls—GAP-01 through GAP-05—to the early-access platform boundaries engineering teams face today. Every custom Python, Valkey, or SQL control in core-cymbal-agent is wrapped in a feature-flagged native adapter hook (CYMBAL_NATIVE_ARD_GA, CYMBAL_NATIVE_KMS_PROBE_GA, CYMBAL_NATIVE_MEM_TTL_GA, CYMBAL_NATIVE_PSC_CUTOVER_GA, and CYMBAL_NATIVE_OTEL_FINOPS_GA) so teams can switch cleanly to native GCP primitives via configuration as they reach general availability. And in row five, our OpenTelemetry FinOps exporter streams SHA-256 prompt hashes and token counters directly into BigQuery so finance teams can run exact SQL chargeback queries across cached and thinking tokens with zero raw PII.
